newsitem.title: USA: S3 buys Faroudja stake for computer video.
newsitem.headline: S3 buys Faroudja stake for computer video.

text.p: Computer chip maker S3 Inc. said Wednesday it bought a stake in video equipment maker Faroudja Laboratories and will use Faroudja's expertise to bring movie-quality video to personal computers.
The price of the purchase was not disclosed.
The companies will work together to develop chips that would let people watch movies and television broadcasts through personal computer monitors.
PC monitors can display images and video much more clearly than regular television sets. But they lose their clarity when displaying TV video signals because of differences in format.
Faroudja, a closely held maker of home theatre equipment, has figured out several ways to increase the resolution of ordinary TV signals.

S3, which specialises in making graphics chips for PCs, will license Faroudja's technology and develop chips around it that would let PCs display high-quality video from digital television broadcasters, satellite TV services or digital versatile disk, or DVD, players, the companies said.
The licensing agreement is part of S3's strategy to pursue the emerging market for devices that merge the power of the PC with the TV, said S3 Chief Executive Gary Johnson.
"We're going to bring the home theatre experience to the PC," Johnson said.
Stock in S3, based in Santa Clara, Calif., jumped $1.50 to $13 in afternoon trading on Nasdaq.
